subject: Numeracy
title: Show what we know again
objectives: Children will show Term 2 learning through play stations.
Teachers will gather evidence for every child’s Term 2 record.
content: Revising comparing and counting, joining and taking away, and shapes and patterns, with end-of-term records.
teachingActivities: Keep every activity familiar and joyful; observe quietly during play; record how far each child counts and how well they join and take away; share records with parents in plain language with a strength, a next step and a home idea.
learnerActivities: Show learning from the term through play stations and a celebration.
assessment: Observe and record each child’s Term 2 numeracy learning.
expectedOutcomes: Completes familiar tasks with growing independence.
Each child has an observation record for Term 2.

lessons.title: Revising comparing and counting
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will revisit more and fewer, one more and less and counting beyond ten through games.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt comparing, one more and less, counting to 15, number order, making five, joining and taking away, shapes and patterns.
lessons.starter: Sing the counting song and say "Today we play our favourite counting games."
teacherActivities: Play more or fewer with two plates.
Play one more and one less on the number line.
Count groups beyond ten with a ten frame.
Let each child choose a favourite game.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play more or fewer with two plates. Children: Child says more or fewer.
Step 2. Teacher: Play one more and one less on the number line. Children: Child steps forward and back.
Step 3. Teacher: Count groups beyond ten with a ten frame. Children: Child counts ten and more.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a favourite game. Children: Child chooses and plays.

practical.title: Counting games
steps: Children play each for five minutes.
practical.safety: Supervise each area and use large counters. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Play beside the child with numbers up to five.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a game.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is one more than six?

expectedOutcomes: Compares groups and counts beyond ten
Finds one more and one less
lessons.conclusion: Count to fifteen and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep playing counting games at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit more and fewer, one more and less and counting beyond ten through games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?

lessons.title: Revising joining and taking away
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will revisit making five, joining and taking away through games.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt comparing, one more and less, counting to 15, number order, making five, joining and taking away, shapes and patterns.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we join and take away in our favourite games."
teacherActivities: Play ducks in the pond to join and take away.
Make five on a five frame with two colours.
Let each child choose a game.
learnerActivities: Child joins and takes away ducks.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play ducks in the pond to join and take away. Children: Child joins and takes away ducks.
Step 2. Teacher: Make five on a five frame with two colours. Children: Child makes five.
Step 3. Teacher: Play the bus story. Children: Child acts the story.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a game. Children: Child chooses and plays.

practical.title: Join and take away games
steps: Children play each for five minutes.
practical.safety: Supervise each area and use large toys. Keep floors clear and chairs steady.

differentiation.support: Play beside the child with groups of three.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a story to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is five take away two?

expectedOutcomes: Joins and takes away with confidence
lessons.conclusion: Put the toys away and wave goodbye.

lessons.title: Maths stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s Term 2 numeracy at play stations.
successCriteria: Shows counting, joining, shape and pattern knowledge
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt comparing, one more and less, counting to 15, number order, making five, joining and taking away, shapes and patterns.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we visit six maths stations and show what we know."
teacherActivities: Set up six stations: comparing, counting, joining, taking away, shapes and patterns.
Observe each child at two stations and record what they do.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up six stations: comparing, counting, joining, taking away, shapes and patterns. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: Observe each child at two stations and record what they do. Children: Children play at stations.
Step 3. Teacher: Take photographs and make notes. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Maths stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station with an adult or helper. Keep floors clear and use large safe materials only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and stay at familiar stations.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to show friends how a station works.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: compares groups; counts beyond ten; one more and less; joins; takes away; names five shapes; continues patterns.

expectedOutcomes: Shows familiar maths skills at stations
lessons.conclusion: Say well done to everyone and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a favourite maths game at home during the holiday.

lessons.title: Revising shapes and patterns

objectives: Children will revisit five shapes and patterns through games.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt comparing, one more and less, counting to 15, number order, making five, joining and taking away, shapes and patterns.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we play shape and pattern games."
teacherActivities: Play the feely bag with five shapes.
Continue an AB pattern with cubes.
learnerActivities: Child feels and names a shape.
Child makes a train from shapes.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play the feely bag with five shapes. Children: Child feels and names a shape.
Step 2. Teacher: Continue an AB pattern with cubes. Children: Child continues the pattern.
Step 3. Teacher: Make a shape train. Children: Child makes a train from shapes.
Step 4. Teacher: Make a bead pattern. Children: Child threads a pattern.

practical.title: Shape and pattern games
steps: Children play each for five minutes.
practical.safety: Supervise each area and use large smooth shapes and beads. Wash hands after glue.

differentiation.support: Play beside the child with three shapes.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a pattern with shapes.

lessons.title: Term celebration and records
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will celebrate Term 2 with songs and games, and teachers will complete each child’s record.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt comparing, one more and less, counting to 15, number order, making five, joining and taking away, shapes and patterns.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we celebrate our term. Let us sing our favourite number songs."
teacherActivities: Sing favourite number rhymes with actions.
Give each child a sticker and say their name.
Complete each child’s record and next step.
learnerActivities: Child waves and says thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing favourite number rhymes with actions. Children: Children sing and do actions.
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child a sticker and say their name. Children: Child waves and says thank you.
Step 3. Teacher: Complete each child’s record and next step. Children: Children play quietly.

practical.title: Celebration circle
practical.safety: Check for allergies before any snack and use non-toxic stickers. Keep the floor clear and supervise all play.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and sing together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose the last song.

assessment.method: Complete each child’s Term 2 numeracy record from the term’s observations. Note the highest number counted accurately, a strength, a next step and a home idea for parents.

questions.question: What is your favourite number game?

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say "See you next term."
lessons.homeConnection: Share the Term 2 record and keep counting over the holiday.
